intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day longtail boat tour around the stunning Phi Phi archipelago, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters at Maya Bay, exploring Viking Cave, and swimming at Monkey Beach. Witness dramatic limestone karsts and vibrant coral reefs teeming with tropical fish.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Market Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Bangkok's legendary street food scene at Yaowarat Road (Chinatown), sampling pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, boat noodles, and fresh oyster omelets. Join a guided walking tour or explore independently through the bustling night stalls and aromatic food carts.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Sunset Beach Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle through serene mangrove forests and sea caves along Koh Lanta's coastline before arriving at a secluded beach to watch a breathtaking Andaman Sea sunset. This guided kayaking experience offers a peaceful alternative to busier islands with stunning natural scenery.

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Sunday Walking Street Food & Culture Experience
experiences.description: Wander through the vibrant Sunday Night Market along Wualai Road, tasting northern Thai specialties like khao soi, sai oua sausage, and kanom krok coconut pancakes. Browse handcrafted goods, watch traditional Lanna cultural performances, and soak in the ancient city atmosphere.
experiences.location: Wualai Road, Old City, Chiang Mai

experiences.name: Koh Samui to Koh Tao Multi-Island Ferry Hop
experiences.description: Take the scenic ferry route from Koh Samui to Koh Phangan and onward to Koh Tao, spending time on each island's distinct beaches. Snorkel at Shark Bay on Koh Tao, relax on Haad Rin Beach on Koh Phangan, and enjoy fresh seafood at beachside restaurants along the way.
experiences.location: Gulf of Thailand — Koh Samui, Koh Phangan & Koh Tao, Surat Thani Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, exchange currency at the airport for a decent rate (avoid hotel exchange counters). Take a budget minivan or shared shuttle to the ferry pier (Rassada Pier in Phuket or Ao Nang in Krabi depending on routing). Board the afternoon ferry to Phi Phi Islands (approx. 1.5–2 hrs). Check in to your Boutique Stay on Phi Phi Don. Drop bags, freshen up, and take a slow walk along the main village strip to get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Tonsai Village on foot — browse the lively night market stalls and beachfront restaurants. Enjoy a casual welcome dinner at one of the open-air street food spots near the pier. Watch the sunset from Tonsai Beach with a cheap Chang beer from a convenience store (7-Eleven is budget-friendly).

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport — 7-Eleven or airport food court (budget ~100–150 THB)
meals.lunch: Airport food court or ferry pier food stall — pad thai or fried rice (~80–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village night market — try green curry with rice, mango sticky rice, and fresh fruit skewers (~150–200 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first evening light — you've had a long travel day. Download the Grab app for transport. Bring cash as many small vendors on Phi Phi don't accept cards. Ferry tickets from Phuket to Phi Phi cost approximately 350–450 THB one way.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–45 min uphill walk from Tonsai Village, entrance fee ~30 THB). The panoramic view of the twin bays is stunning and best enjoyed before the heat peaks. Take photos, then descend and grab breakfast from a local bakery or street stall near the pier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Long Beach (Haad Yao) on the southeast side of Phi Phi Don — reachable by a short longtail boat ride (~50–80 THB) or a 20-minute walk at low tide. Spend the afternoon swimming and snorkeling in the clear turquoise water. Long Beach is quieter and less crowded than Tonsai. Bring your own snorkel gear if possible, or rent cheaply on the beach (~100 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village for a street food dinner. Stroll the evening market and sample local skewers, som tum (papaya salad), and fresh coconut ice cream. Enjoy the laid-back fire show performances that happen nightly on the beach — free to watch.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery near Tonsai pier — banana pancake and fresh juice (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Beach shack at Long Beach — fried rice or noodle soup (~100–130 THB)
meals.dinner: Tonsai street food market — som tum, grilled satay skewers, pad see ew (~150–180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: October is shoulder/low season — expect occasional rain showers in the afternoon. Carry a small rain poncho. The viewpoint hike is best done before 9:00 AM to avoid heat and crowds. Wear sturdy sandals or sneakers for the hike.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group snorkeling tour around Phi Phi Leh (the smaller uninhabited island). Tours depart around 8:30–9:00 AM from Tonsai Pier and typically cost 400–600 THB per person including snorkel gear. Visit Maya Bay (famous from 'The Beach' film), Pileh Lagoon, Viking Cave, and Monkey Beach. Book through a guesthouse or local tour desk the evening before for the best price.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the tour around 13:00–14:00. Have lunch in the village, then spend the afternoon relaxing on Tonsai Beach or Loh Dalum Bay. Loh Dalum is the stunning crescent bay on the north side — perfect for a lazy swim. Rent a kayak (~200 THB/hour) to paddle along the bay's edge.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at one of the cliff-side bars overlooking Loh Dalum Bay — many offer happy hour deals (buy-one-get-one cocktails). Dinner at a slightly nicer beachfront restaurant — treat yourself to fresh grilled fish or seafood for a modest splurge.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or 7-Eleven — toast, eggs, coffee (~60–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Village noodle shop — boat noodles or wonton soup (~80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant on Loh Dalum — grilled sea bass with rice and vegetables (~250–350 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Group snorkeling tours are the most budget-friendly way to see Phi Phi Leh. Private longtail charters cost significantly more. Maya Bay has a daily visitor cap and entrance fee (~400 THB) which is usually included in tour prices — confirm before booking.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning longtail boat to Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai), a small island north of Phi Phi Don known for its pristine white sand and excellent snorkeling. Longtail charters can be shared with other travelers to split costs (~150–200 THB per person each way). Arrive early before day-trippers from Phuket arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a few hours snorkeling and swimming at Bamboo Island. Return to Phi Phi Don by early afternoon. Visit the small local market near the school area of Tonsai Village — away from the tourist strip — for cheap authentic Thai snacks and fresh fruit.
day_by_day.evening: Take a free sunset walk along the Tonsai beachfront. Join a budget cooking class if available (~500–700 THB) — some guesthouses and local restaurants offer evening classes where you learn to make 2–3 Thai dishes and then eat your creation for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Street stall near pier — rice porridge (jok) with egg and ginger (~60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Bamboo Island beach shack or packed lunch from village (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner or local restaurant — massaman curry and jasmine rice (~150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Bamboo Island is best visited on a calm weather day — check conditions the night before. The island has basic facilities only. Bring sunscreen, water, and snacks. October weather can be unpredictable so have a backup plan.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your accommodation and take the morning ferry from Phi Phi Don to Krabi Town (approx. 1.5 hrs, ~250–300 THB). Arrive mid-morning and check in to a budget guesthouse or hostel in Krabi Town (dorms from ~250 THB, private rooms from ~400–600 THB). Drop bags and explore Krabi Town's riverside walking street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — a 30-minute songthaew ride from town (~40–60 THB). Climb the 1,237 steps to the summit for breathtaking views over Krabi's limestone karsts and coastline. The climb takes 45–60 minutes and is free to enter (modest dress required). Descend and explore the cave temple at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Krabi Town Night Market (open evenings near the riverside) — one of the best budget food spots in southern Thailand. Sample local southern Thai cuisine including massaman curry, roti with condensed milk, and fresh seafood. Stroll the riverside promenade and watch the longtail boats on the Krabi River.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast on Phi Phi before ferry — fruit smoothie and toast (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Krabi Town local restaurant near the market — khao man gai (chicken rice) (~70–90 THB)
meals.dinner: Krabi Night Market — 3–4 dishes and drinks (~150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is very steep — wear proper shoes and bring water. Not recommended during heavy rain. Songthaews (shared red trucks) are the cheapest local transport in Krabi at 40–60 THB per trip. Grab bikes are also available.

day_by_day.morning: Take a songthaew to Ao Nang Beach (~40 THB, 20 mins from Krabi Town). Ao Nang is the main beach resort area and a hub for island-hopping excursions. Walk along the beachfront promenade and browse tour operators for deals on the Four Islands Tour — compare prices at multiple shops (budget ~600–800 THB per person for a full-day group tour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the Four Islands Tour departing from Ao Nang (~10:00 AM or 13:00 PM). Visit Koh Poda, Koh Gai (Chicken Island), Koh Tub, and Koh Mor — all featuring stunning beaches, snorkeling, and the famous sandbar that appears at low tide connecting the islands. Snorkel gear included. Return to Ao Nang by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ao Nang's evening street food scene along the main road — cheaper than beachfront restaurants. Try fresh grilled prawns, papaya salad, and mango sticky rice from market stalls. Return to Krabi Town by songthaew for a cheaper overnight stay.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse or local café in Krabi Town — eggs, toast, coffee (~80–120 THB)
meals.lunch: Included in Four Islands Tour or pack your own snacks
meals.dinner: Ao Nang street food stalls — grilled seafood, pad thai, fresh coconut (~180–220 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The Four Islands sandbar experience is tide-dependent — best at low tide. Confirm timing with your tour operator. Book tours early in the morning for same-day departures. Ao Nang is more expensive than Krabi Town for food and accommodation — stay in town and day-trip for best budget value.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang to Railay Beach (15 mins, ~100 THB each way) — Railay is only accessible by boat due to surrounding limestone cliffs. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Explore Railay West Beach (calm, good for swimming) and Railay East Beach (mangroves, longtail docks).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike to Phra Nang Cave and Princess Cave on the southern tip of the Railay peninsula — free and spectacular. Swim at Phra Nang Beach, consistently rated one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches. For the adventurous: attempt the Railay Viewpoint hike (steep jungle trail, ~45 mins, free) for panoramic karst views. Rent a kayak (~200 THB/hour) to explore the sea caves and lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset from Railay West Beach before taking the last longtail back to Ao Nang. Head back to Krabi Town for dinner. Visit the local fresh market near Maharaj Road for ultra-cheap Thai food eaten with locals.

meals.breakfast: Ao Nang street stall — roti with egg and banana (~60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Railay Beach shack — fried rice or noodles (~120–150 THB, slightly pricier due to island location)
meals.dinner: Krabi Town local market — authentic southern Thai curry over rice (~80–100 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Railay has no ATMs — bring sufficient cash. Prices on Railay are higher than Krabi Town due to its remote location. The Viewpoint hike involves rope-climbing sections and can be muddy — not suitable in heavy rain. Wear shoes with grip.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget bus or minivan from Krabi to Koh Lanta (~2.5 hrs, 200–250 THB via ferry crossing included). Depart by 9:00 AM. Arrive on Koh Lanta Yai (the main island) and check in to a budget bungalow or guesthouse on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) — the most popular and well-connected beach. Bungalows start from ~400–600 THB per night.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a motorbike (~200–250 THB/day) — the best and cheapest way to explore Koh Lanta's long coastline. Ride south along the main road, stopping at Klong Nin Beach (quieter, local vibe) and Kantiang Bay (stunning bay with budget restaurants). Visit the Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Si Raya) — a charming stilted fishing village with Chinese-Thai heritage shophouses along the water.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the west-facing beaches — Klong Nin or Kantiang Bay offer spectacular views. Return to Long Beach area for dinner at one of the casual beachfront restaurants with fairy lights and floor cushions.

meals.breakfast: Krabi Town — rice porridge or toast before departure (~60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Old Town seafood restaurant — fresh fish and rice (~150–180 THB)
meals.dinner: Long Beach beachfront restaurant — green curry, rice, Chang beer (~200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Motorbike rental requires a valid license (international driving permit recommended). Drive carefully — roads can be wet and hilly. Koh Lanta is more relaxed and less touristy than Phi Phi — great for budget travelers. Fill up on petrol at roadside stalls (~35–40 THB/liter).

day_by_day.morning: Ride your motorbike to the southern tip of the island to visit Mu Ko Lanta National Park (entrance fee ~200 THB). Explore the lighthouse trail through jungle to a clifftop lighthouse with sweeping sea views. Spot monitor lizards and tropical birds. The park also has a small beach and coral reef for snorkeling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget snorkeling day trip from Koh Lanta to the nearby islands of Koh Rok and Koh Ha — known for some of the best underwater visibility in the Andaman Sea. Group tours depart from the pier near Long Beach (~800–1,000 THB including snorkel gear, lunch, and park fees). Alternatively, relax on Bamboo Bay or Waterfall Bay for a free afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Long Beach for a relaxed evening. Find a beachside bar with hammocks and enjoy happy hour (often 17:00–19:00 with 2-for-1 cocktails at ~150–200 THB). Dinner at a cheap local restaurant set back from the beach (avoid beachfront markup).

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café — eggs, toast, fruit (~100–130 THB)
meals.lunch: Included in island tour or National Park food stall (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant off the beach road — pad kra pao (basil stir fry) with rice and fried egg (~100–130 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok and Koh Ha tours are best booked a day in advance. October may see some rain — the national park can be muddy. The southern end of Koh Lanta gets very few tourists — a rewarding experience for budget travelers who want authentic atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a lazy morning on Long Beach or Klong Dao Beach — one of the longest and most beautiful beaches on Koh Lanta. Swim, read, or rent a paddleboard (~300 THB/hour). Explore the local morning market near the main road for cheap fresh fruit, Thai pastries, and local snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lanta Animal Welfare center — a non-profit dog and cat shelter that welcomes volunteers and visitors (donations appreciated). Then explore the central part of the island by motorbike — stop at local rubber and palm plantations, a small temple, and a freshwater waterfall (seasonal — may be flowing well in October after rains).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koh Lanta Old Town for a final evening stroll along the wooden pier walkway. Browse handicraft shops and local art galleries. Dine at one of the Old Town's riverside restaurants — fresh seafood at local prices. Return to your guesthouse and pack for tomorrow's journey.

meals.breakfast: Morning market — fresh fruit, sticky rice with mango, Thai iced coffee (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Roadside local restaurant near center of island — khao pad (fried rice) with pork or shrimp (~80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Old Town riverside restaurant — grilled barracuda or red snapper with rice and vegetables (~200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Lanta Animal Welfare is a great way to give back during your trip. The waterfall is only accessible by motorbike or on foot — ask your guesthouse for current conditions. Old Town is a UNESCO-listed area and worth visiting at golden hour for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Koh Lanta guesthouse and take the minivan/ferry combination back to Krabi (~2.5 hrs). From Krabi, take an onward bus or minivan to Koh Samui via Surat Thani (total journey ~5–6 hrs by bus + ferry, ~350–500 THB) OR fly budget airline (AirAsia/Nok Air from Krabi to Koh Samui, ~800–1,500 THB if booked in advance). Arrive on Koh Samui and check in to a budget guesthouse near Chaweng or Lamai Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: After arriving and settling in, take a songthaew to Chaweng Beach — the island's most famous and lively beach. Walk the 7km beach strip, swim in the Gulf of Thailand waters, and browse the beachside shops. Visit the Chaweng Lake area inland for cheaper food and local life away from the tourist strip.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Chaweng's famous Walking Street night market for cheap street food, souvenirs, and live entertainment. Sample local Samui specialties like grilled fresh coconut, seafood BBQ, and Thai desserts. The night market is lively, colorful, and very budget-friendly.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Koh Lanta before departure — fruit and yogurt (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Bus/ferry journey — pack snacks or buy at Surat Thani bus station (~80–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Chaweng Walking Street night market — pad thai, satay, fresh coconut, mango sticky rice (~150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The overland + ferry route to Koh Samui is the most budget-friendly option. Book minivan + ferry combination tickets from travel agents in Krabi Town the day before. Flying saves time but costs more. October is low season on Samui — expect good deals on accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike (~200 THB/day) and do a self-guided island tour of Koh Samui. Start with the famous Big Buddha Temple (Wat Phra Yai) in the north — free entry, stunning 12-meter golden Buddha. Continue to Fisherman's Village in Bophut — a charming old Chinese-Thai village with boutique shops and local cafés along the waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Na Muang Waterfalls in the island's interior — two beautiful waterfalls accessible by motorbike (free entry to Waterfall 1, ~200 THB for Waterfall 2 which requires an ATV or hike). Swim in the natural pools beneath the falls. Continue to Lamai Beach on the south coast — quieter than Chaweng, with the quirky Grandmother and Grandfather Rocks (Hin Ta Hin Yai) nearby — free and amusing natural rock formations.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset from Lamai Beach or the western coast viewpoints. Head back toward Chaweng for a final evening out — enjoy a beachfire BBQ dinner at one of the budget beachfront spots. Try local Samui-style yellow curry and fresh grilled prawns.

meals.breakfast: Bophut Fisherman's Village café — coffee and eggs on toast (~120–150 THB)
meals.lunch: Waterfall area food stall or roadside restaurant — fried noodles or rice with pork (~80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Lamai or Chaweng beachfront BBQ restaurant — grilled seafood platter with rice (~250–300 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Na Muang Waterfalls can be slippery — wear proper footwear. The road to Waterfall 2 is steep and unpaved — assess your motorbike confidence first. Fisherman's Village hosts a Friday Night Walking Street market — if your visit aligns, it's one of the best markets in Samui.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Samui. If time allows before departure logistics, visit the Wat Plai Laem Temple — a colorful, multi-armed deity statue on a lake, free to visit and stunning for photography. Alternatively, spend a final relaxed morning on Chaweng or Lamai Beach for one last swim in the Gulf of Thailand. Grab a Thai iced coffee and fresh fruit from a street cart.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of accommodation and head to Koh Samui Airport or the ferry pier for onward travel. If flying home from Bangkok, take the budget ferry to Surat Thani and then a bus/train to Bangkok (overnight train ~300–500 THB in 2nd class sleeper is a great budget option), or fly direct from Samui (~1,000–2,000 THB). Use remaining Thai Baht on last-minute street food, snacks, and small souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or transit evening. If transiting through Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi Airport, explore the airport's food court for authentic and cheap Thai food (much better value than international terminal restaurants). Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, islands, and street food across southern Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Final street food breakfast — banana pancake, fresh fruit shake, Thai iced tea (~100–120 THB)
meals.lunch: Chaweng local restaurant or airport food court — khao man gai or green curry (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Airport food court or transit meal — pad thai or tom yum soup (~120–180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Budget approximately 500–1,000 THB for last-day transport, tips, and any remaining purchases. Keep some cash for airport departure tax if applicable (usually included in ticket price). Exchange remaining Baht back to home currency at the airport or keep for a future trip — Thai Baht is stable and widely accepted at exchange counters globally.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and collect luggage. Take a shared minivan or taxi to Rassada Pier in Phuket Town, then board a high-speed ferry to Phi Phi Islands (approx. 1.5–2 hour journey). Check into your boutique stay and freshen up. Take a gentle stroll along Tonsai Village to get oriented — explore the narrow pedestrian lanes, souvenir shops, and waterfront views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Tonsai beachfront area to watch the sunset over the Andaman Sea. Explore the lively but relaxed night atmosphere of Tonsai Village.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or meal at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: Airport or ferry terminal food court — try a simple Thai rice dish or noodle soup (approx. 80–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Papaya Restaurant on Phi Phi — a mid-range local favorite offering Thai classics like pad thai, green curry, and fresh seafood (approx. 200–400 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry schedules from Rassada Pier to Phi Phi run until around 17:30–18:00. If arrival is delayed, consider an overnight stay in Phuket and take the first morning ferry. Book your boutique stay transfer in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and walk to Tonsai Beach for a sunrise stroll. Rent a kayak (approx. 200–300 THB/hour) and paddle along the coastline toward Loh Dalum Bay, enjoying the dramatic limestone cliffs and crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day snorkeling longtail boat trip to nearby Phi Phi Leh — visit the famous Maya Bay (check current access rules), Pileh Lagoon, and Viking Cave. Snorkel among colorful reef fish and coral (tours approx. 500–800 THB per person).
day_by_day.evening: Climb the Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–40 minute hike, entrance fee ~30 THB) for a breathtaking panoramic view of both bays at golden hour. Return to Tonsai for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a Western or Thai breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café — try khao tom (rice porridge) or toast with eggs (100–180 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or eat at a beachside shack on Phi Phi Leh — fresh coconut and fruit skewers are ideal
meals.dinner: Unni's Restaurant, Tonsai Village — beloved mid-range spot with excellent Thai and international fusion dishes, great cocktails (300–500 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted visitor hours and capacity limits to protect the ecosystem. Confirm current regulations with your tour operator. October weather may bring occasional rain showers — carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Hire a private longtail boat for a half-day island hopping adventure to Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai) — known for its white sandy beach, shallow turquoise water, and excellent snorkeling. Arrive early before day-trippers (longtail charter approx. 1,500–2,000 THB for the boat).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phi Phi Don and spend the afternoon relaxing on Loh Dalum Bay beach. Try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP rental approx. 300 THB/hour) or simply swim and sunbathe on the crescent-shaped beach.
day_by_day.evening: Join a fire show on the beach — Loh Dalum Bay has nightly fire dancers and beachside bars with a fun, festive atmosphere. Enjoy a cocktail while watching the performance.

meals.breakfast: Street food breakfast near Tonsai pier — try roti with banana and condensed milk or fresh fruit smoothies (60–120 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a simple restaurant on Loh Dalum Bay — grilled fish, som tam (papaya salad), and sticky rice (150–250 THB)
meals.dinner: Cosmic Restaurant & Bar, Phi Phi — popular mid-range spot with a mix of Thai and Western food, great for groups and solo travelers (250–450 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate longtail boat prices at the pier the evening before or early morning for better rates. Bamboo Island is a protected marine park — bring reef-safe sunscreen and avoid touching coral.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Phi Phi to Ao Nang, Krabi (approx. 1.5 hours, 350–450 THB). Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Ao Nang for one night. Walk along Ao Nang Beach and explore the beachfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a 4-island longtail boat tour from Ao Nang — visit Tup Island (walkable sandbar at low tide), Chicken Island (Koh Kai), Poda Island (Koh Poda), and Mor Island. Snorkel, swim, and enjoy the dramatic karst scenery (tours approx. 500–700 THB per person).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang and explore the night market on the main strip. Browse local handicrafts, clothing, and street food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Tonsai pier café before ferry departure — toast, eggs, and coffee (100–150 THB)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch included in most 4-island tour packages, or buy snacks from beachside vendors on the islands
meals.dinner: Ao Nang Night Market — sample street food classics: pad see ew, mango sticky rice, grilled satay sticks, and fresh spring rolls (150–300 THB for a full spread)

day_by_day.notes: The 4-island tour is tide-dependent — the famous Tup Island sandbar is only accessible at low tide. Check tide times with your tour operator. Book tours at the Ao Nang beachfront pier for competitive prices.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang to Railay Beach (15–20 minutes, 100 THB each way) — this stunning beach is only accessible by boat due to surrounding limestone cliffs. Explore Railay West and Railay East beaches, and hike to the Railay Viewpoint for panoramic cliff-top views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Phra Nang Cave Beach — one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches with a sacred princess cave shrine. Swim in the emerald waters and explore the cave interior. Try rock climbing on the famous limestone cliffs of Railay (beginner courses available, approx. 800–1,200 THB with instructor).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang by longtail boat. Catch a tuk-tuk to Krabi Town (30 minutes) and check into a guesthouse near the night market for the next two nights.

meals.breakfast: Ao Nang beachfront café — American breakfast or Thai-style congee with side dishes (120–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Railay Beach Restaurant — fresh seafood and Thai curries with a stunning beach view (200–350 THB per person)
meals.dinner: Krabi Town Night Market (Maharaj Road) — an authentic local street food market with incredible variety: khao pad, tom yum soup, grilled corn, and Thai desserts (100–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Railay is car-free and boat-only. Last longtail boats back to Ao Nang run until around 18:00–19:00 depending on season. Phra Nang Cave is a sacred site — dress respectfully near the shrine area.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Krabi Town's riverside area — walk along the Krabi River promenade and visit the quirky Krabi Town Walking Street (weekends) or the morning fresh market. Visit Wat Kaew Korawaram, a stunning white Buddhist temple in the center of town (free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a songthaew (shared truck taxi) to Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb the famous 1,237 steps to the summit for a spectacular 360-degree view of Krabi Province. Allow 1.5–2 hours for the round trip. Entrance is free but bring water and wear comfortable shoes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town and explore the evening riverside market. Enjoy a relaxed evening watching the sunset over the mangroves from the riverside pier.

meals.breakfast: Krabi Town morning market — try khao man gai (poached chicken rice) or kuay teow (noodle soup) from local vendors (50–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Tiger Cave Temple — simple Thai rice dishes and fresh-squeezed juices (100–200 THB)
meals.dinner: May & Mark Restaurant, Krabi Town — a beloved local gem serving authentic southern Thai cuisine including massaman curry, crab stir-fry, and fresh fish (200–400 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — avoid midday heat. October may bring afternoon rain; the climb can be slippery when wet. Modest dress required at the temple (cover shoulders and knees).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a minivan or ferry from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approx. 2–3 hours including ferry crossing, 350–500 THB). Check into a mid-range beachfront bungalow on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao). Settle in and take a morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter (approx. 200–300 THB/day) and explore Koh Lanta Old Town — a charming stilted sea village with Malay-Chinese heritage, colorful wooden shophouses, art galleries, and local cafés. Browse boutique shops and learn about the island's multicultural history.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Sunset Point on the western coast of Koh Lanta for one of Thailand's most spectacular sunsets. Many beach bars and restaurants set up along the coast for golden hour viewing.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Krabi minivan terminal or pack snacks for the journey
meals.lunch: Koh Lanta Old Town café — try fresh seafood with rice or a Thai-Muslim yellow curry (150–250 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant on Long Beach — grilled whole fish, prawn pad thai, and fresh coconut (250–450 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta is more relaxed and less touristy than Phi Phi — perfect for a mid-trip reset. Scooter rental requires an international driving license; always wear a helmet. October is shoulder season — some restaurants may have reduced hours.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day snorkeling and island hopping tour from Koh Lanta to the Trang Islands — visit Koh Rok (a stunning marine national park with vibrant coral reefs) and Koh Ha (five-island cluster with caves and excellent visibility). One of Thailand's best snorkeling destinations (tours approx. 1,200–1,800 THB including park fees).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling at Koh Ha — explore underwater caves and swim through natural arches. Look for leopard sharks, sea turtles, and diverse reef fish. Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on Long Beach and watch the sunset. Enjoy a beachside massage from one of the many affordable spa shacks along the beach (Thai massage approx. 250–350 THB/hour).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or beachfront café — fruit bowls, eggs, and coffee (100–180 THB)
meals.lunch: Included in most Koh Rok/Koh Ha tour packages — typically a Thai lunch served on the boat or island
meals.dinner: Drunken Sailors Bar & Restaurant, Long Beach — casual mid-range spot with fresh seafood BBQ and cold beers, popular with travelers (250–400 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok is a national marine park — entrance fees apply (approx. 400 THB for foreigners). Reef-safe sunscreen is mandatory. Book tours through your guesthouse or at the Saladan pier for best prices.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Koh Lanta by scooter — ride south along the coast to Koh Lanta National Park (entrance 200 THB). Hike through the jungle to a lighthouse with stunning coastal views. Look for wildlife including monitor lizards and macaques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Khlong Nin Beach on the way back — a beautiful, quieter beach with a more local vibe. Swim and relax before heading back toward Saladan. Visit a local rubber plantation or take a short mangrove kayaking tour (approx. 400–600 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Long Beach for your final evening on Koh Lanta. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a beachfront restaurant and stargaze from the beach.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or Long Beach café — smoothie bowls and toast (120–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Khlong Nin Beach restaurant — simple Thai lunch with a sea view, try the local fish curry (150–250 THB)
meals.dinner: Time for Lime Restaurant, Koh Lanta — a social enterprise cooking school and restaurant using local ingredients; excellent Thai food with a meaningful story (300–500 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: The road to Koh Lanta National Park can be rough in parts — drive carefully on a scooter. Pack water and snacks for the national park hike. Book the next day's transport to Phuket in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a ferry and minivan combination from Koh Lanta to Phuket (approx. 3–4 hours, 500–700 THB). Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Patong or Kata Beach area. Freshen up and head to the beach for a swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Patong Beach or Kata Beach — both offer water sports, beach clubs, and a lively atmosphere. Try parasailing (approx. 500–800 THB) or jet skiing for an adrenaline boost. Walk the beachfront promenade and browse shops.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Bangla Road in Patong for the famous night market atmosphere — street food, live music bars, and vibrant street performances. Sample street food snacks without committing to the full party scene if preferred.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Koh Lanta before departure — roti with egg and tea (80–120 THB)
meals.lunch: Phuket-style lunch at a local restaurant near your guesthouse — try Phuket-style hokkien noodles or dim sum (100–200 THB)
meals.dinner: Kata Mama Restaurant, Kata Beach — a legendary local spot with outstanding Thai home cooking at very reasonable prices (150–300 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Phuket is more commercial than Phi Phi or Koh Lanta — embrace the energy but stay aware of tourist traps. Tuk-tuks in Phuket are notoriously expensive; use Grab app for fairer prices.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Phuket Old Town — explore the beautifully preserved Sino-Portuguese architecture, vibrant street murals, and boutique coffee shops along Thalang Road and Soi Rommanee. Visit the Phuket Thai Hua Museum to learn about the island's Chinese heritage (entrance 200 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day cooking class in Phuket Town — learn to make 4–5 authentic Thai dishes including Phuket-style dishes like mee sua (yellow noodles) and gaeng som (sour curry). Classes typically include a market visit (approx. 1,200–1,800 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Return to your beach area and enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar or beachside bar. Explore the Phuket Weekend Night Market (Naka Market) if visiting on a weekend for excellent local street food and shopping.

meals.breakfast: Phuket Old Town café — try o-tao (oyster pancake) or khanom jeen (fermented rice noodles with curry) at a heritage café (100–180 THB)
meals.lunch: Cooking class lunch — eat what you cook! Typically a full spread of Thai dishes
meals.dinner: Roti Chao Fa, Phuket Town — a famous street-side roti stall serving sweet and savory roti variations; pair with a nearby curry stall (100–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot in the morning before the heat peaks. Many Old Town cafés and shops are closed on Mondays — plan accordingly. The cooking class market visit is a fantastic street food education.

day_by_day.morning: Take a speedboat day trip to the Similan Islands (if weather and season permit — check with operators as Similans may be closed Oct–Nov) OR alternatively join a full-day tour to Phang Nga Bay — explore the iconic James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), sea caves, and floating Muslim fishing villages by longtail boat or kayak (tours approx. 1,200–1,800 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Phang Nga Bay tour — kayak through dramatic limestone caves and mangrove tunnels, and visit Koh Panyee, the famous floating village built on stilts, for lunch and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phuket by late afternoon. Enjoy a final beachside dinner and a leisurely walk along your chosen beach at sunset. Treat yourself to a traditional Thai massage to soothe travel-weary muscles (350–500 THB/hour at a reputable spa).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or beachfront café — eggs, fresh fruit, and coffee (120–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Koh Panyee floating village restaurant — fresh seafood with rice, a unique dining experience (150–300 THB)
meals.dinner: Suay Restaurant, Phuket — a celebrated mid-range restaurant blending Thai and international flavors with beautiful presentation; perfect for a special final evening (400–700 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Similan Islands National Park is typically closed from May to October for environmental protection — confirm status with operators. Phang Nga Bay is an excellent alternative with equally stunning scenery. Book tours the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and last swim at the beach. Pack and check out of your guesthouse. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping: pick up Thai spices, coconut products, silk scarves, or local handicrafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, visit Big Buddha (Phra Phutta Ming Mongkol Eknakiri) — a 45-meter white marble statue on Nakkerd Hill with panoramic island views (free entry, donations welcome). A peaceful and meaningful final experience in Thailand.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Phuket International Airport for departure. Arrive at least 2–3 hours before your flight. Enjoy a final Thai meal at the airport and reflect on 13 incredible days in the Land of Smiles.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — khao tom (rice soup) with pork or a full hotel breakfast (100–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Big Buddha or at a local restaurant en route to the airport (150–250 THB)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or food court — try one last bowl of tom kha gai (coconut milk soup) or pad kra pao (basil stir-fry) before departure (150–300 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport transfer — Phuket traffic can be heavy, especially during peak hours. Keep some Thai Baht for airport snacks and final tips. Most hotels offer luggage storage if your flight is late evening. Duty-free at Phuket Airport has good deals on Thai spirits and tea.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at destination airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat transfer from Krabi or Phuket pier to Phi Phi Islands. Check in to your boutique luxury property, unwind on the private terrace, and enjoy a welcome drink while soaking in panoramic Andaman Sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel's clifftop or beachfront bar, followed by a leisurely orientation stroll along Tonsai Bay's vibrant waterfront promenade to get your bearings on the island.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or at the departure airport
meals.lunch: Light bites at the hotel upon arrival — fresh tropical fruit platter, coconut water, and a club sandwich
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant, Phi Phi — a beloved fine-casual spot renowned for fresh seafood, authentic Thai curries, and grilled fish with sea views

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your speedboat transfer in advance through the hotel concierge for a seamless arrival experience. October marks the tail end of the rainy season — seas are generally calm but carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat tour to Maya Bay (The Beach) — arrive early before day-trippers for an exclusive experience. Snorkel the crystal-clear waters of Loh Samah Bay and explore the limestone karst formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Island hopping to Bamboo Island and Monkey Beach. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by your hotel on a secluded stretch of white sand. Snorkeling gear provided for vibrant coral reef exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don, freshen up, then enjoy a traditional Thai cooking class at a premium local venue — learn to prepare Pad Thai, Tom Kha Gai, and Mango Sticky Rice.

meals.breakfast: Full Thai breakfast at the hotel — congee, fresh papaya, eggs your way, and freshly brewed Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic box on Bamboo Island — grilled prawns, som tam salad, artisan sandwiches, and chilled coconut
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Grand Bleu, Phi Phi — upscale French-Thai fusion restaurant with fresh catch of the day and panoramic sea views

day_by_day.notes: Book your private longtail boat through the hotel concierge the night before. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and underwater camera for snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike to Phi Phi Viewpoint (Viewpoint 1 and 2) — the most iconic panoramic vista in the islands. A guided 20-minute hike rewards you with sweeping views over both bays. Photography golden hour at its finest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking adventure through the sea caves and hidden lagoons of Phi Phi Leh. Explore Pileh Lagoon, a stunning emerald-green enclosed bay accessible only by kayak or small boat.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront fire show and cultural performance at Tonsai Bay, then a relaxed evening stroll through the night market for artisan souvenirs and local crafts.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-hike breakfast at the hotel — energy bars, fresh fruit, and Thai iced tea
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at Ciao Bella, Phi Phi — wood-fired pizzas, fresh grilled squid, and cold-pressed juices overlooking the bay
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dining experience arranged by your hotel — candlelit table on the sand, multi-course Thai tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The viewpoint hike is best done at sunrise (around 06:00) for cooler temperatures and dramatic light. Wear sturdy sandals or trail shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Scuba diving excursion with a certified PADI dive center — explore Hin Daeng and Hin Muang dive sites, among Thailand's best, known for leopard sharks, manta rays, and vibrant coral walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phi Phi Don, relax with a traditional Thai massage at the hotel spa. Enjoy the infinity pool with Andaman Sea views and read or nap in a private cabana.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on a private chartered longtail boat around Phi Phi Leh — champagne, canapés, and a professional photographer to capture the golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at the hotel — tropical fruits, eggs benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and smoothie bar
meals.lunch: Post-dive recovery lunch at the dive center's café — hearty Thai noodle soup, green papaya salad, and fresh lime soda
meals.dinner: Dinner at Papaya Restaurant, Phi Phi — renowned for authentic Southern Thai cuisine, massaman curry, and fresh whole fish steamed in lime and chili

day_by_day.notes: Confirm diving certifications in advance. Non-divers can opt for a snorkeling tour to the same sites. The private sunset cruise should be booked 24 hours ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Premium speedboat transfer to Railay Beach, Krabi — one of Thailand's most dramatic and beautiful beaches, accessible only by boat. Explore Railay East and West beaches, and the iconic Phra Nang Cave Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rock climbing session on Railay's world-famous limestone karst cliffs with a certified guide — suitable for beginners and experienced climbers alike. Alternatively, kayak through the mangrove forests.
day_by_day.evening: Return by speedboat to Phi Phi Islands. Enjoy a wellness sunset yoga session on the hotel's private beach terrace followed by a relaxing herbal steam bath at the spa.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — light continental spread with Thai-style congee and fresh tropical juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at Railay Beach Bar & Restaurant — fresh seafood platters, green curry, and chilled Singha beer with beachfront views
meals.dinner: In-hotel fine dining — Chef's special tasting menu featuring Southern Thai flavors, fresh Andaman seafood, and Thai dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: The speedboat to Railay departs from Tonsai pier. Journey takes approximately 45 minutes. Wear swimwear under clothes for easy beach access.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium island hopping tour departs early — visit the Four Islands of Krabi: Koh Lanta Noi, Koh Ngai (Hai), Koh Mook (with the magical Emerald Cave), and Koh Kradan. Swim through the dark sea cave to reach the hidden beach inside Emerald Cave.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling at Koh Kradan's pristine house reef, consistently ranked among Thailand's top snorkeling spots. Relax on powdery white sand with a cold drink from the boat's cooler.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Islands. Enjoy a street food evening walk — explore local vendors for Moo Ping (grilled pork skewers), Roti with banana and condensed milk, and fresh-squeezed sugarcane juice.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — grab-and-go option with pastries, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch on the boat — grilled chicken, sticky rice, som tam, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Street food tour self-guided around Tonsai Village — budget 500–800 THB per person for an authentic spread of local delicacies

day_by_day.notes: The Four Islands tour is a full day — depart by 08:00. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed. Emerald Cave entry requires swimming in darkness for about 80 meters — thrilling but safe.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning — sleep in, enjoy a long hotel breakfast, and spend time at the pool or private beach. Optional early morning stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) session in the calm bay waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat transfer to Koh Lanta — a larger, more laid-back island with pristine beaches. Explore the charming Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta), a historic Sino-Portuguese fishing village with colorful wooden shophouses over the water.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Koh Lanta before returning to Phi Phi by private speedboat. Alternatively, consider a one-night extension at a luxury resort on Koh Lanta for a change of scenery.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full hotel breakfast — eggs to order, fresh juices, and Thai-style dishes
meals.lunch: Lunch at Time for Lime, Koh Lanta — a celebrated cooking school and restaurant with fresh, organic Thai cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mango House, Koh Lanta Old Town — atmospheric waterfront restaurant with fresh seafood and Thai-Western fusion

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta Old Town is a UNESCO-recognized heritage area. Respectful dress is appreciated when visiting the local mosque and community areas. Arrange return speedboat by 20:00.

day_by_day.morning: Guided cultural morning — visit a local Thai fishing village near Phi Phi for an authentic community experience. Learn about traditional fishing techniques, visit a local temple, and interact with residents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium spa afternoon at the hotel — indulge in a 90-minute traditional Thai herbal compress massage followed by a 60-minute facial using local botanical ingredients. Relax by the pool afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the hotel bar with live acoustic Thai music. Enjoy the last golden light over the Andaman Sea before a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Thai and Western spread
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — fresh spring rolls, grilled tiger prawns, and a chilled coconut smoothie
meals.dinner: Premium sushi and seafood omakase experience at a curated restaurant in Tonsai — pre-booked tasting menu with sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: The spa treatments should be booked at least one day in advance through the hotel concierge. This is an ideal rest and recovery day after a week of active exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning boat trip to Shark Point (Hin Musang) — one of the best snorkeling and diving spots near Phi Phi, teeming with blacktip reef sharks, sea turtles, and colorful reef fish. A truly unforgettable marine wildlife experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phi Phi Don. Explore the local street food scene at Tonsai Market — sample Thai iced tea, fresh coconut ice cream, grilled corn, and mango sticky rice. Browse local artisan stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfire gathering on a private section of beach arranged by the hotel — bonfire, cold drinks, and stargazing on a clear Andaman night.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-excursion breakfast at the hotel — light but energizing: bananas, yogurt, granola, and coffee
meals.lunch: Street food lunch at Tonsai Market — 400–600 THB per person for a variety of local dishes
meals.dinner: Romantic private beach dinner arranged by the hotel — Thai BBQ seafood feast with fresh lobster, prawns, and whole fish, served with wine

day_by_day.notes: Shark Point is best visited at high tide. Reef sharks are harmless and the experience is awe-inspiring. Bring an underwater camera or GoPro.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by premium speedboat to Phuket — check in to a luxury clifftop resort in Kata Noi or Surin Beach area for a two-night stay. Explore the resort facilities and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Promthep Cape — Phuket's most famous viewpoint, offering dramatic panoramas over the southern tip of the island. Continue to Rawai Beach to browse the seafood market and watch longtail boats.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Phuket Old Town — a UNESCO-listed historic district with stunning Sino-Portuguese architecture, vibrant street art, and an excellent night market. Sample local Phuket-style street food.

meals.breakfast: Final Phi Phi hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bampot Kitchen & Bar, Phuket Old Town — farm-to-table Thai cuisine in a beautifully restored heritage shophouse
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Phuket Walking Street Night Market — try Mee Hokkien (Phuket-style noodles), Satay, and fresh oysters

day_by_day.notes: The speedboat from Phi Phi to Phuket takes approximately 1.5 hours. Arrange luxury resort transfer from Rassada Pier in advance. Pre-book your Phuket accommodation for 2 nights.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat tour to the Similan Islands (if weather permits) — a UNESCO-protected marine park considered one of the world's top 10 dive and snorkel destinations. Crystal-clear waters, giant boulders, and diverse marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phuket. Afternoon at leisure on Surin Beach or Kamala Beach — two of Phuket's most upscale and beautiful stretches of sand. Enjoy a beachside massage from a licensed therapist.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise around Phang Nga Bay on a luxury catamaran — champagne, canapés, fresh seafood dinner, and spectacular views of the iconic limestone karsts including James Bond Island.

meals.breakfast: Full luxury hotel breakfast — extensive buffet with live cooking stations, fresh juices, and Thai specialties
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch on the Similan Islands boat — fresh sandwiches, tropical fruit, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Catamaran sunset dinner cruise — multi-course Thai and international menu with wine and cocktail pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Similan Islands tour departs from Thap Lamu Pier (2 hours from Phuket). Confirm weather conditions the night before. This is an absolute highlight not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Elephant sanctuary visit — spend a meaningful morning at an ethical elephant sanctuary near Phuket. Feed, bathe, and walk alongside rescued elephants in a responsible, no-riding environment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phuket. Indulge in a luxury afternoon tea at the Sala Phuket or Trisara resort — elegant Thai-inspired pastries, finger sandwiches, and premium teas overlooking the Andaman Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a world-class Phuket restaurant — PRU Restaurant (one of Thailand's best farm-to-table fine dining experiences, Michelin-recognized) or Acqua Restaurant for Italian-Thai fusion with panoramic views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — light and fresh before the sanctuary visit
meals.lunch: Post-sanctuary lunch at a local Phuket restaurant — Khao Man Gai (Hainanese chicken rice), Tom Yum Goong, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: PRU Restaurant, Phuket — Michelin-starred tasting menu with locally sourced, seasonal ingredients and expert wine pairing. Budget approximately 4,000–6,000 THB per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the ethical elephant sanctuary well in advance as spots are limited. PRU Restaurant requires reservations made at least 1 week ahead. This is your final full evening — savor every moment.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk or swim at your Phuket beach. Last Thai breakfast at the hotel. Pack and check out — arrange private luxury transfer to Phuket International Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Phuket International Airport. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for international departure. Browse duty-free for Thai silk, artisan goods, and premium Thai tea and coffee.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at transit hub. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Thai beaches, island hopping, and culinary discovery.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast at the hotel — Jok (rice porridge), fresh tropical fruit, Thai tea, and eggs
meals.lunch: Light airport lunch at a premium lounge or airside restaurant — Thai green curry or noodle soup
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at transit airport

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from your Phuket hotel if your flight departs in the afternoon or evening. Purchase Thai souvenirs such as premium jasmine rice, artisan silk scarves, and handcrafted ceramics from airport boutiques. Ensure all receipts are kept for VAT refund at the airport.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
